text: I pressed my nose against the frosted window, desperate to see what moved beyond.

Something about the way the lock clicked made my mind whirl.

I nudged the drawer open, hungry for the secrets it kept.

The way she paused mid-sentence left me burning with questions.
I stared at the photograph, sure it held more than it showed.
Something clicked when I saw the footprints vanish into thin air.
I couldn’t resist peeking inside the envelope marked 'DO NOT OPEN'.
The rustling in the leaves made me hold my breath and listen.
My fingers hovered above the ancient keys, yearning to know their tune.
The flicker in her eyes told a story I had to hear.
I leaned over the balcony, wondering what lay just out of view.
The symbol carved into the stone made my skin tingle with wonder.
My gaze fixed on the locked chest, heart racing with anticipation.
I bent closer to the mirror, startled by what wasn’t my reflection.
That one unread message sat there, begging to be opened.
Even the silence seemed full of questions I needed answered.
I leaned closer to the painting, certain I saw it move.
The way he hesitated on that word lit up my imagination.
I poked the strange foam, wondering if it was alive.
The hum behind the wall made my thoughts spiral with theories.
I heard the glass shatter and didn’t even turn my head.
Someone called my name, and I barely lifted my eyes.
The mail stacked up, and I stepped over it again.
I missed my stop and didn’t bother getting off.
He cried beside me, and I just stared at the wall.
The plants turned brown, and I kept scrolling through my feed.
They argued across the room, but I couldn’t be bothered to care.
The wind blew the papers away, and I watched them scatter.
Even hunger felt like too much effort to acknowledge.
I ignored the ringing doorbell and stayed curled on the couch.
The dishes stacked high, but I didn’t lift a finger.
He told me his dream, and I just blinked at the ceiling.
They lit candles for me, and I stared at the floor.
The room filled with music, but I felt nothing.
I missed the bus and didn’t mind waiting in the rain.
They handed me a gift, and I mumbled without opening it.
The candle burned down to nothing, and I didn’t replace it.
I sat through the meeting and remembered none of it.
Laughter rang out nearby, and I turned the volume up.
The power went out, and I just kept staring into the dark.
The milk spoiled, and I poured it anyway.
He stormed out, and I didn’t even look up.
The parade passed, and I yawned without looking.
My shoelace snapped, and I kept walking.
The toast burned, and I ate it anyway.
